domestic.debt_note: Latest MTB auction (2026-07-08): govt raised Rs2,067.9bn vs a Rs2.4tn target; cutoffs eased 31-40bps across the curve -- 1M 11.3968%, 3M 11.3978%, 6M 11.4375%, 12M 11.4880% -- all sub the 11.5% policy rate, i.e. the market is pricing an eventual cut (https://propakistani.pk/2026/07/08/govt-borrows-rs-2-trillion-from-local-debt-market/). PIB 10Y last read 11.69% at the 2026-07-06 settlement of the 2026-07-02 auction (Rs516.67bn bid, Rs112.5bn accepted at the 10Y tenor); no fresher PIB print found this run (https://tradingeconomics.com/pakistan/government-bond-yield). No new weekly reserves print found beyond 2026-07-10 this run.
domestic.remittances: FY26 closed at a record $41.6bn (+8.6% YoY vs $38.3bn in FY25). June 2026 alone was $3.48bn, easing off May's record $4.25bn but roughly flat YoY vs June 2025's $3.4bn; Saudi Arabia ($829.6mn), UAE ($792.2mn), UK ($514.9mn), US ($296.8mn) the top corridors (https://www.thenews.pk/story/1424957-fy26-remittances-hit-416bn-showing-86-yearly-growth)
domestic.current_account: FY26 full-year current account posted a marginal $139mn deficit, reversing FY25's $1.84bn surplus, despite the remittance record -- driven by high imports against stagnant exports. June 2026 alone was a $649mn deficit vs a $500mn surplus in May 2026 and a $220mn surplus in June 2025 (https://dailytimes.com.pk/1524687/pakistan-posts-139m-current-account-deficit-despite-record-remittances-in-fy26/, https://tribune.com.pk/story/2618897/ca-slips-into-649m-deficit-1)

global_read: global.json (21:37) shows Brent pushing to a fresh cycle high of $91.06 (+2.06% 1d, +16.89% 1mo) and WTI $84.27 (+1.25%/+12.63%), the dominant PSX-specific transmission channel via the import bill, PKR and reserves. Equities and vol have eased from yesterday's tape -- S&P +0.92%, Dow +0.95%, VIX down sharply -8.47% to 17.07 -- suggesting the acute global panic phase has cooled even as oil keeps climbing. PKR/USD flat-ish at 277.64 (+0.48% 1d), DXY 101.12 (+0.13% 1d). Net: global risk appetite is no longer the binding constraint today: it is the oil-driven domestic channel (import bill, reserves, inflation, PKR) that still argues for caution into the 2026-07-27 MPC.
drivers: SBP policy rate held at 11.5% at the 2026-06-15 MPC (final FY26 review). Next MPC -- first of FY27 -- is confirmed for 2026-07-27; independently checked beyond the news-sentinel flag, a Topline Securities survey reported by both propakistani.pk (2026-07-21) and BOL News shows 97% of respondents expect a hold at 11.5% and 3% expect a 100bp cut, citing heightened geopolitical uncertainty and the recent oil rebound despite contained inflation; 49% see rates still at 11.5% by December 2026 vs 46% expecting cuts (https://propakistani.pk/2026/07/21/sbp-likely-to-keep-interest-rate-unchanged/, https://www.bolnews.com/business/sbp-expected-to-hold-interest-rate-steady-amid-geopolitical-uncertainty-poll-shows/, https://www.techjuice.pk/sbp-to-announce-first-monetary-policy-decision-of-fy27-on-july-27/)

CPI eased to 11.1% YoY in June 2026 from 11.7% in May (still far above 3.2% a year earlier); urban 11.2%, rural 10.9%; MoM CPI fell 0.3%; trimmed-mean core 9.6% urban / 9.3% rural, both down slightly but still elevated. FY26 average inflation 7.05% vs 4.49% in FY25. July print not yet released by PBS as of today (due ~2026-08-01) (https://english.news.cn/asiapacific/20260702/c7990325ef774005bea4071d441354e3/c.html, https://www.pbs.gov.pk/price-statistics/)

IMF EFF/RSF program on track: 3rd EFF review + 2nd RSF review completed 2026-05-08, disbursing ~$1.1bn (EFF) + ~$220mn (RSF); FY26 primary surplus of 1.6% of GDP reported in line with targets amid a 'challenging global environment, including the ongoing Middle East war' -- the IMF's own language flags the same geopolitical channel this desk is pricing (https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2026/05/08/pr-26147-pakistan-imf-completes-3rd-rev-of-extended-arrangement-under-eff-and-2nd-rev-arrang-rsf)

SBP FX reserves fell $1.245bn w/w to $17.226bn for the week ended 2026-07-10 (from $18.471bn) on external debt repayments; total liquid reserves $22.676bn (from $23.988bn). No fresher weekly print (e.g. week ended 2026-07-17) was found this run despite a dedicated search -- reserve trajectory since remains the last verified read (https://tribune.com.pk/story/2618658/reserves-down-124b-on-debt-repayments, https://propakistani.pk/2026/07/16/sbp-reserves-crash-after-big-debt-payment/)

Latest T-bill auction (2026-07-08): govt raised Rs2,067.9bn vs a Rs2.4tn target; cutoffs eased 31-40bps across tenors, all below the 11.5% policy rate (1M 11.3968%, 3M 11.3978%, 6M 11.4375%, 12M 11.4880%) -- the market is still pricing an eventual cut even as the MPC itself is expected to hold on 07-27 (https://propakistani.pk/2026/07/08/govt-borrows-rs-2-trillion-from-local-debt-market/)

FY26 closed with a record $41.6bn in remittances (+8.6% YoY) but the full-year current account nonetheless slipped to a marginal $139mn deficit (from a $1.84bn FY25 surplus), with June alone posting a $649mn deficit on high imports against flat exports -- a genuine (if small) external-account deterioration alongside the reserve drawdown (https://dailytimes.com.pk/1524687/pakistan-posts-139m-current-account-deficit-despite-record-remittances-in-fy26/, https://www.thenews.pk/story/1424957-fy26-remittances-hit-416bn-showing-86-yearly-growth)

Desk geo-risk radar (state/georisk.json, updated 21:37) reads 63/100 'moderate', but its two largest sub-factors -- conflict/escalation (100/100, still tied to the live US-Iran/Strait of Hormuz situation) and energy shock via Brent (90/100, up from 79 the prior run as Brent pushes to a fresh $91 cycle high) -- are both pinned at or near maximum stress. Per desk practice this argues against a risk-on call even though the composite band itself reads only 'moderate', and even though the pure equity/VIX tape (global.json) has cooled from yesterday (state/georisk.json)

Net regime read: a cooling global equity/vol tape is offset by an intensifying oil-driven domestic channel (fresh Brent highs, ongoing reserve drawdown, a newly-deficit current account) heading into the 2026-07-27 MPC where a hold is all but priced in -- kept at risk-off rather than upgraded to neutral
